objective: Match the snapshot manifest's database label against the exact supported backend set on EventStore.restore and refuse anything else, so recovery never guesses a parser and never opens a snapshot under storage semantics it was not written for.
acceptance: database must be exactly 'sqlite' or 'jsonl'; a missing, unknown, misspelt or non-string value is refused
a sqlite-labelled snapshot is never opened with the JSONL parser
a jsonl-labelled snapshot is never opened as SQLite and remains replay-equivalent
the refusal happens before any destination write or replacement, so pre-existing destination bytes survive unchanged
existing backup/restore round trips and the schema, hash and event-count checks still pass
the refusal is an EventStoreError that names the unsupported backend, not a raw sqlite3 driver error
evidence: focused test output for the supported pair and for the missing, unknown, misspelt and wrong-type labels
demonstration that the backend-identity tests fail against the previous fall-through-to-jsonl implementation and pass against the fix
byte-identical destination evidence for a refused restore that targets an existing store
confirmation that the pre-existing snapshot, restore and recovery tests still pass unchanged
stop_conditions: an existing snapshot has to be migrated or rewritten; an explicit version bump is a separate decision
a new storage backend is added or a supported snapshot format changes
a modification outside allowed_paths is required
a live store, robot control or firmware path becomes involved
